hero.title: Many brands. One codebase.
hero.subtitle: I build token architectures where a new brand is one file of 55 values. Components, markup and releases stay exactly the same. The proof is below: a live product in 4 brands and 2 themes.

demo.title: Switch the brand. The code stays put.
demo.lead: Pick Aurum, Nova, Fiesta or Ultra, then flip light and dark. Colors, fonts, radii and spacing change. The components underneath don't.

architecture.title: Six layers. Only one of them is the brand.
architecture.lead: A component never knows which brand it is in. It asks for a meaning, the theme picks a step on a color ramp, and only the brand file holds real colors, fonts and radii. Every number below is counted from the demo's tokens at build time.

components.name: Components
components.detail: Buttons, cards and chips read meanings, never raw values.

theme.name: Theme
theme.detail: Semantic colors: text, fill, border. Light and dark are an axis of their own.

typography.name: Typography
typography.detail: Built from the brand's fonts and the core type scale.

map.name: Map
map.detail: Tints and shades calculated from brand colors, so nobody picks them by hand.

brand.name: Brand
brand.detail: The only file that changes when you add a brand.

core.name: Core
core.detail: The raw scale: sizes, radii, weights, base colors.

explorer.title: Follow one token through the layers
explorer.themeNote: Switch the site theme at the top right: light and dark take different steps of the same ramp.

notes.base: step 500 is the brand color itself

how.title: How a brand gets from Figma to production

steps.title: A brand is data
steps.detail: Every brand is one Token Studio file with the same 55 keys: colors, fonts, radii, spacing, layout. Designers change values. Component tokens are never touched.

steps.title: The pipeline builds it
steps.detail: Tokens live in Git as JSON and compile to CSS custom properties. Automated checks catch missing keys, broken layer references and failing WCAG contrast before anything ships.

steps.title: Two attributes switch it
steps.detail: The product changes brand and theme with data-brand and data-theme on one element. Same markup, same components, one release for every brand.

audience.title: For teams running more than one brand

items.title: iGaming and white-label platforms
items.detail: One product sold under many brands. Every operator gets its own look without a separate codebase.

items.title: Fintech with sub-brands
items.detail: A main brand plus products for different audiences or markets. Same UX, different look, one library.

items.title: Agencies on one stack
items.detail: Many clients on the same components. A new client starts from a brand file, not from a fork.
